Corpus-wide, a standalone "gze" token occurs in exactly 4 segments: C03:322, C16:404 and P1:15 are the same sentence repeated verbatim (byte-identical wylie and English across all three), and the fourth, C11:469 ("...mi bzod pa'i gze re can du 'gyur ba..."), is the unrelated word "gze re can" — i.e. "gze" never functions as a verb of repaying kindness anywhere in the corpus except this one recurring sentence. "drin gzo" (the correct spelling) occurs in 28 other segments. Checked directly against the entries table: the headword "gze" exists with hgm_gloss = [] (empty — it entered the lexicon from this corpus reading alone and defines nothing), while "gzo" glosses as ["to wish to repay","repay","repaying"] and "drin gzo" as ["to wish to repay that kindness","repaying their kindness","repay kindness","wish to repay that kindness"]. No standard form of gzo ba has an e vowel. The English ("pay this kindness back") is unaffected and correct; only the Wylie/ACIP is defective, so the span for this word is left unkeyed rather than banking "gze = pay" as a lexeme.
